title: Sreeshankar and Sathyanathan Both Qualify for CWG Long Jump Final as India's Athletics Campaign Opens Strong
excerpt: Murali Sreeshankar breached the automatic qualifying mark with his first jump, while Lokesh Sathyanathan made the top 12 to give India two shots at a medal in Glasgow.
body:
• Murali Sreeshankar cleared the 8.00m automatic qualification mark with his very first jump of 8.01m, finishing third overall in the qualifying round.
  • Lokesh Sathyanathan jumped 7.77m to finish seventh overall and qualify as one of the top 12 — giving India two finalists.
  • The men's long jump final is scheduled for July 29 in Glasgow.
  • Sreeshankar is attempting to better the silver medal he won at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games after recovering from a ruptured patellar tendon that cost him the Paris Olympics.

India will have two athletes in the men's long jump final at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games after Murali Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan both qualified on the opening day of the athletics programme on Sunday.

Sreeshankar, the reigning Commonwealth Games silver medallist, needed just one jump. His opening-round leap of 8.01 metres cleared the automatic qualification standard of 8.00m, finishing third overall behind Jamaica's Tajay Gayle (8.10m) and Saint Vincent's Uroy Ryan (8.04m). He did not need to take his remaining two attempts.

Sreeshankar's Comeback Continues

The 27-year-old's composed performance belied the difficulty of his journey back to this stage. In April 2024, Sreeshankar suffered a ruptured patellar tendon — a career-threatening injury that ruled him out of the Paris Olympics and left his competitive future in doubt.

He returned to competition gradually, and by June this year had jumped 8.38 metres at the National Inter-State Senior Athletics Championship in Bhubaneswar — his season's best and a distance that places him among the favourites for a medal on Tuesday. At the 2022 Birmingham Games, he took silver with a jump of 8.08m.

Sathyanathan Earns His Spot

If Sreeshankar's qualification was expected, Sathyanathan's was a significant bonus. The 24-year-old produced his best effort of 7.77 metres on his first attempt in Group B, then fouled on his second and third jumps. But the opening mark was enough to place him seventh overall and comfortably inside the top 12 qualifiers.

Having two Indians in the final deepens India's medal chances and creates tactical flexibility — a luxury the country has rarely enjoyed in track and field events at the Commonwealth level.

Mixed Results Elsewhere on Day One

The athletics session produced other bright spots for India. Tejas Shirse advanced to the men's 110-metre hurdles final, clocking 13.76 seconds to finish third in his heat. Swimmer Sajan Prakash also qualified for the men's 200-metre butterfly final with a time of 1:58.59.

The session's biggest disappointment came in the men's 100 metres, where national record holder Gurindervir Singh was eliminated in the opening round. Competing in Heat 4, the sprinter clocked 10.39 seconds — good for second in his heat but only 28th overall out of the 17 athletes who advanced to the semi-finals.

Looking Ahead to Tuesday's Final

The men's long jump final is scheduled for the evening session on July 29 at Scotstoun Stadium. Sreeshankar's season form suggests he is capable of challenging for gold, though Gayle — the Commonwealth record holder at 8.69 metres — enters as a formidable opponent.

For Sreeshankar, the final represents more than a medal opportunity. A podium finish would cap one of Indian athletics' most compelling comeback stories and confirm his return to the top tier of global long jumpers after an injury that might have ended a lesser career.
